limitations: Every component identity and engineering fact in these examples comes from an installed synthetic test-fixture catalog.
The examples contain no reviewed or admitted production profile and make no orderability claim.
No live provider, price, stock, lifecycle, lead-time, or other commercial response is included.
Behavioral circuits and analytic outputs are deterministic regression examples, not selected-part or simulator-fidelity evidence.

assumptions.description: Loss and efficiency are evaluated at 80% PWM duty and the declared 1.5 A continuous rating under a steady-state load.
Winding resistance is estimated as 12 V divided by 5 A stall current.
Winding inductance, back-EMF constant, and target speed are unavailable, so startup and speed-dependent simulations are not eligible.
No user current-limit target is imposed; device safety limits remain hard constraints.
The reference fixture uses a 125 °C maximum estimated junction temperature.
This electrical reference request deliberately omits live sourcing; sourcing behavior is covered by separate synthetic fixtures.

meta.description: Editable averaged operating-point model: static ideal bridge switches, effective capacitors, winding R/L where supplied, and an explicit operating-point back-EMF source. It does not model PWM edges, selected-part silicon, speed/torque dynamics, protection, thermal behavior, or PCB parasitics. Gate-driver control, gate resistors, pull-downs, and bootstrap parts remain in the candidate BOM but are not representable on these static two-terminal switches.

limitations: The averaged static bridge does not express commutated braking or decay transients
Explicitly averaged model: the bridge rail is nominal supply multiplied by declared duty cycle
Four static ideal 1 mΩ/1 GΩ switches show one forward conduction state; PWM edges, dead time, switching loss and selected-part silicon are not simulated
Back-EMF is an algebraic operating-point closure, not evidence for a motor constant
Behavioral netlist generation is tested; no native-ngspice/WASM numerical-validation claim is made
Static ideal switches do not express driver current-limit/protection behavior
Winding inductance, back-EMF constant, or target speed is missing from the request
The candidate carries one averaged operating-point circuit and no scenario-specific startup circuit/config

warnings: Behavioral back-EMF is an algebraic operating-point closure, not evidence for a physical motor constant
Circuit is an averaged steady-state behavioral bridge with static ideal switches, not selected-part silicon or switching simulation
Dynamic motor parameters are incomplete; startup and speed-dependent simulation are unavailable
Motor winding resistance is estimated from nominal voltage and stall current
Synthetic fixture component profiles are not reviewed real parts and are not orderable

assumptions.description: Loss and efficiency are evaluated at 80% PWM duty and the declared 1.5 A continuous rating under a steady-state load.
Winding resistance is estimated as 12 V divided by 5 A stall current.
Winding inductance, back-EMF constant, and target speed are unavailable, so startup and speed-dependent simulations are not eligible.
No user current-limit target is imposed; device safety limits remain hard constraints.
The reference fixture uses a 125 °C maximum estimated junction temperature.
This electrical reference request deliberately omits live sourcing; sourcing behavior is covered by separate synthetic fixtures.
